items.name: chat
items.title: Chat
items.author: Jamie Thompson <jamie@jamiethompson.design> (https://jamiethompson.design)
items.description: AI chat block for AI SDK useChat: a MessageScroller transcript that follows streamed output, an Empty state with one-click Suggestions, user text in Bubbles, assistant parts as Message Response (Streamdown), Reasoning, Tool (tool-* and dynamic-tool) and Attachments, a shimmering Marker while a request is pending, an error row with Retry on failure, and a Prompt Input composer with attachments whose submit button becomes Stop while a response is in flight (given onStop). Ships as a composable Chat component (plus ChatMessages, ChatMessage, ChatMessagePart, ChatToolPart, ChatAttachments, ChatEmpty, ChatThinkingMarker, ChatErrorMarker and ChatComposer exports), a scripted demo conversation built with @shadcn/helpers createChat that streams with no API key, and an app/chat page wiring it up. Use it to start a chatbot, assistant or agent UI, then swap the demo transport for your own route.
items.docs: Built for the Base UI styles (base-nova): it composes the base-nova wrappers from components/ui and the @uifiles AI items, which rely on Base UI's render prop and event signatures, so it does not work on Radix or React Aria styles. The page installs at app/chat/page.tsx and streams a scripted conversation through @shadcn/helpers, so it works without an API key. To connect a model, replace `transport` in the page with `new DefaultChatTransport({ api: "/api/chat" })` from `ai` and add a route that returns `result.toUIMessageStreamResponse()`. Pass `error` and `onRetry={regenerate}` from `useChat` so a failed request renders a row with its message and a Retry button; when `status` is "error" and no `error` is given the row still appears with a generic "Something went wrong." (Retry only when `onRetry` is passed), and a rejected `onRetry` (`regenerate` rejects when there is nothing to regenerate) is reported through `console.error`, never as an unhandled rejection; after an error the composer shows a plain Submit again. While a response is in flight, Enter, the submit button and a programmatic `form.requestSubmit()` submit nothing and the draft and attachments are kept (ChatComposer returns `false` from `onSubmit`); if you pass `onStop` to Chat or ChatComposer (the page passes `stop` from `useChat`) the submit button becomes a Stop button that calls it, and without `onStop` it keeps the Submit name and a press does nothing. The page does not return `sendMessage`'s promise from `onSubmit` (it settles only once the answer has streamed) and ChatComposer does not wait for it either, so sent attachments leave the composer as soon as the message is sent and a file attached while an answer streams stays. If your `onSubmit` returns a promise that rejects, from the composer or a suggestion click, the rejection is reported through `console.error`, never as an unhandled rejection; if it throws synchronously the error is reported the same way and the composer keeps the draft and attachments. Once the chat is no longer generating (after Stop, or a stream that ended early) parts still marked streaming or running are shown settled, and a tool call left in input-available reads Pending; a tool call whose input has not started shows the Tool item's "No input yet" placeholder. Approval-requested tool calls are shown but not wired: compose @uifiles/confirmation with `addToolApprovalResponse` from `useChat` to add human-in-the-loop approvals. Chat fills its parent: render it inside a height-constrained container (the page uses h-svh). Suggestions are submitted as-is when clicked. CSS: the CLI adds @uifiles/response's stylesheet lines to your globals.css with this block: `@import "streamdown/styles.css"`, `@import "katex/dist/katex.min.css"` (without it every formula renders twice) and the `.katex-display` overflow rule. Add `@source "../node_modules/streamdown/dist/*.js"` yourself, next to your `@import "tailwindcss"` and with the path relative to your CSS file, so Streamdown's Tailwind classes compile. See @uifiles/response for what each line does.
